mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% in the month prior to the decision point reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) using a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 20,000 jobs in the prior month correlates with stronger consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During periods of high unemployment, the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the prior month's average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods orders) grows by more than 10% in the prior quarter, it indicates accelerating business activity that anticipates stronger earnings and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In contractionary quarters, the 60-day forward return does not exceed the 10% quantile of past expansion quarters (quantile test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 5% suggests supply-side constraints, which can lead to higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During periods of normal production growth, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (unemployment rate) above historical averages in the prior month create a dual signal of higher policy costs and weaker labor market, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
regime_hint: coordinated tightening and labor market stress
failure_condition: In non-coordinated regimes where FEDFUNDS rises but UNRATE does not, the 5-day return is not negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (housing starts) of 10% or more indicates cooling in the housing market, which can reduce consumer wealth and depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: During periods of robust housing growth, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds INDPRO by more than 15 percentage points for two consecutive months, it signals stronger consumer demand than production, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > INDPRO + 0.15 * INDPRO for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In periods where RSAFS < INDPRO by any margin, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a low-unemployment, high-inflation environment (UNRATE < 4% and CPIAUCSL > 3% over the prior 3 months) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to expectations of tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% over the last 3 months
failure_condition: During non-inflationary regimes (UNRATE > 4%), the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
